name: google_search_camoufox
description: UPDATE 2026-09-05: timeout_ms 45000 -> 34000 (per-phase; see test_builtin_timeout_fits_the_first_attempt). The 45000 figures below are the 2026-08-28 state. Google web search (organic results). Returns one flat array per field across organic results; consumers zip them by index. ROW-ALIGNMENT INVARIANT: every field must match exactly one node per result, so all four scope to #rso div.tF2Cxc — the organic-result container Google renders for EVERY result (div.g was retired) — which also keeps ads/PAA/nav blocks out. `snippets` anchors to div.tF2Cxc itself (not to div[data-sncf='1'], which exists ONLY when the result has a snippet) and digs the text out of that container's html by regex: a snippet-less result then yields null in its own slot instead of shrinking the array and silently shifting every later row up one. Never point a field at an element that only exists when its value does. UPDATE 2026-09-04 -- `links` ARE FOLLOWABLE AGAIN, and `display_urls` is added. Google confirmed on 2026-08-26 that it rewrites every result href to an opaque `/goto?url=` token; the token cannot be decoded, and the CALLER WARNING below describes that RAW href. This preset now (1) reads `display_urls` -- the display URL Google still prints under every title, `<cite>https://www.wired.com › story</cite>` -- from the organic container's html with the same regex + strip_tags recipe `snippets` uses, so a container with no cite yields null IN ITS OWN SLOT rather than shortening the column (each container repeats the cite in a sibling block; the regex takes the first; in the 2026-08-28 capture it sits INSIDE the same `<a>` as the `<h3>`, 8 of 8); and (2) sets `resolve_redirects: ["links"]`, so the worker resolves each stub to its destination after parsing -- the mechanism, its bounds and what it refuses are documented on `ScrapeRequest.resolve_redirects`. Live after deploy: every stub resolved on every run that reached a SERP (research/goto_v2_google_search_chromium.json). WHAT THE WRAPPER MEANS: a source that tested both reports Google serves `/goto` stubs only to sessions it has classified as automated and plain hrefs to ordinary browsing, so the presence of stubs is itself a verdict on the session -- a softer one than /sorry; asset blocking off, `humanize` and an 8 s warmup dwell did not change it (research/google_probe_2026_09_04_direct_links_probe.json). CALLER WARNING (raw href) -- `links` as read from the page ARE NOT FOLLOWABLE DESTINATIONS: every organic href Google serves here is a RELATIVE redirect stub of the form /goto?url=CAES... , not a URL. Nothing recovers the target from it -- the payload is opaque bytes, so no selector change, `urljoin` or `base64_decode` helps. Recorded by an earlier audit, unjudgeable on 2026-08-27 (zero rows on both twins, so no links to inspect), and REPRODUCED on 2026-08-28 once the wait fix below recovered real SERPs: all 23 links across the three google_search_chromium runs that returned rows are /goto?url= stubs (de#0 8/8, de#1 8/8, uk#1 7/7, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json), pinned by tests/presets/test_google_search_interstitial.py::TestRealSerpMarkupStillMatches::test_links_are_the_real_goto_redirect_stubs. `titles` and `snippets` are usable; treat `links` as a row marker, not a destination. This was an open defect until 2026-09-04; it is identical on both engine twins, and both twins now carry the same resolution. Routes to country-specific domain (google.de, google.co.uk, ...) matching the locale's market country (gl=/hl=). The proxy exit follows `proxy_country` where set, not the market: the `us` locale exits via GB because Google blocks this proxy pool's US residential range. Materializer must lowercase `country` for gl= and derive a language code for hl= from the locale. ENGINE: Camoufox, fingerprint_profile=windows_on_host — a Windows claim over this host's real AMD GPU vendor. Windows rather than the honest Linux because measurement put an honest Linux claim at 15 and 23 retries against 1 and 8 for Windows (see src/browser/fingerprint_profile.py). MEASURED 2026-08-27 (n=2 per locale, 6 runs per engine, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): THIS PRESET RETURNED NO DATA ON EITHER VARIANT — 0/6 runs each. This variant did reach the page: 6/6 runs ended on the requested …/search?q=… URL with HTTP 200 and the block heuristic silent, where google_search_chromium ended on google.com/sorry/index 6/6 with all three retries spent. It then extracted nothing: 0 rows and "field 'titles': required selector not found" on all six. ROOT CAUSE SETTLED 2026-08-28 (task 5, by capture): `wait_until: domcontentloaded` returns before the redirect completes — Google serves a JS bounce shell at this stage (91,619 bytes live 2026-08-28/DE; 82 characters of visible body text after stripping script/style — "Klicke hier, wenn du nach einigen Sekunden nicht automatisch weitergeleitet wirst", i.e. "click here if you aren't redirected automatically after a few seconds"; zero #rso, zero h3, zero div.tF2Cxc, zero /goto?url=), not a captcha, not /sorry, not a consent wall. Measured live 2026-08-28: a single fetch with `wait_until: load` (no selector) leaves the shell and resolves the redirect for real — landing on either the SERP or google.com/sorry depending on whether the exit passes Google's JS check — where `domcontentloaded` never observes either outcome, only ever the shell. Fixed the same way `yandex_search` was (read that preset first): `wait_until: load` plus `wait_for_selector: #rso`. This splits into two distinct, correctly-classified outcomes instead of one silent success: if the redirect leaves the page stuck on this shell (URL unchanged, not a recognised block endpoint), `wait_for_selector` genuinely times out and raises `selector_not_found: #rso`, which `is_selector_miss()` (src/queue/scrape_runner.py:132) treats as retry-worthy; if instead it lands on `google.com/sorry`, `redirected_to_block()` (src/browser/camoufox_runner.py:441, mirrored at src/browser/runner.py:1095) recognises the URL BEFORE `wait_for_selector` is ever called, skips the wait entirely (no extra latency over the old config), and the block classifier sets `blocked=True` with `"Captcha/block detected by heuristic"` — rotation then happens on `fetch_result.blocked` (src/queue/scrape_runner.py:646), not on a selector miss. Either way the old domcontentloaded-only config's single silent "0 rows, no error" stop is gone. `timeout_ms` raised 30000->45000 to match the 3-phase (warmup+goto+selector) budget yandex_search already uses; at PAGE_TASK_TIMEOUT_S=120s this fits on the fast-fail path (attempt 1 affordable ≈37.5s of the 45s requested, shortened-and-logged exactly like yandex's own attempt 1) but costs a real attempt: in the pathological case where every phase burns its full timeout, 3 phases afford only ONE full attempt before the 120s ceiling is spent (attempt 2 reported "not started"), where the old 2-phase/30000ms config could still afford two. A genuinely blocked run is not slower, though — see redirected_to_block above; only a run that stays ambiguously stuck (not yet recognised as a block) pays the extra phase's time. This changes `/api/v1/search?engine=google`'s latency too: it pins `google_search_chromium` (src/api/search.py:68) and materializes it with no wait_until/wait_for_selector/timeout_ms override (src/api/search.py:242-248 — `_proxy_override`/`_engine_override` only ever set proxy/engine fields), so a caller there now waits up to ~37.5s longer for a real answer on a clean exit, or the same block-speed dead end on a burned one. This does NOT fix google_search_chromium's access block: that preset's OWN audit figure is 6/6 at /sorry (12/12 was google_search_chromium + google_shopping_chromium COMBINED, not this one), unchanged by this task. It also does not guarantee a clean exit for Camoufox — this proxy pool's exit reputation drifts day to day (15 of 15 live verification attempts across this task on 2026-08-28 ended at /sorry, worse than this preset's own audit figure of 6/6 REACHED / 0/6 blocked one day earlier) — it fixes the fact that the old config could not even tell the difference between a shell, a block and a real SERP. MEASURED 2026-08-28 (retest of the same twenty presets through the same harness after the five audit fixes; n=2 per locale, 92 runs, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json): 0/6 runs returned data -- but THE FAILURE MODE CHANGED, and that change is the fix. On 08-27 all six runs ended on the requested .../search?q=... URL at HTTP 200 with the block heuristic SILENT, 0 rows and "field 'titles': required selector not found": the interstitial shell reported as a clean fetch. On 08-28 all six ended on google.com/sorry with blocked=True and "Captcha/block detected by heuristic" (4 at HTTP 200, 2 at 429), 3 retries each. The preset can no longer report a redirect shell as a successful 200; every 0-row google run in the new record is labelled a block. ACCESS, separately, was worse on this engine than on its Chromium twin today (0/6 here against 3/6 there) -- the exact reverse of 08-27, where this variant reached the page 6/6 and the twin was blocked 6/6. Two runs per locale cannot separate an engine effect from exit reputation, and the reversal across one day is itself evidence that the binding variable is the exit. CALLER TIMEOUT, CONFIRMED: one attempt of this preset now costs ~36s -- every google run in the 08-28 record carries "attempt 1/3 shortened to ~36000ms of the requested 45000ms to fit the page-task ceiling" (measured 35.7-36.4s) -- and a job that spends all three attempts reached took_ms 59058 (google_search_chromium/us) and 57193 (google_search_camoufox/us), before any queue wait. `/api/v1/search?engine=google` materializes google_search_chromium with no wait_until/wait_for_selector/timeout_ms override (src/api/search.py:68 and 242-248), so it inherits these numbers verbatim, and yozh-law-checker's backend/app/services/scraper_search_client.py:27 calls /api/v1/search with `timeout=60` and has four `return None` degrade paths. THAT CLIENT IS NOT AFFECTED TODAY: it calls the endpoint only with engine="yandex", which routes to yandex_search_camoufox and is untouched by this change. The consequence is conditional on that client switching to engine="google", at which point a blocked or retrying Google job legitimately outlives its 60s budget and the caller receives None with nothing to log, indistinguishable from an empty SERP. OPERATOR ACTION, IF AND WHEN THAT SWITCH HAPPENS: raise that client's timeout to at least 90s (clear of the 59.1s worst job measured here, still under PAGE_TASK_TIMEOUT_S=120s), or -- if 60s is a hard product constraint -- log the timeout degrade distinctly so "we gave up waiting" is never reported as "Google returned nothing".
